_comment: Firebird provider -- feature 12 (OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 5; feature doc
012-firebird-provider.md FB-DEC-01 + FB-DEC-02 + FB-DEC-03).
Firebird is the hardest adapter Tina4 ships: no generic last_insert_id (a
GENERATOR/sequence assigns the key), an asymmetric identifier case-fold, a
native C client no socket timeout reaches, and blob columns that must be read
OUT of a handle. This fixture pins the write-path + resilience behaviours a
caller depends on against a REAL Firebird 5 :3050 (SYSDBA -> the per-framework
tina4_<fw>.fdb), no mocks. Under TINA4_REQUIRE_SERVICES a skip here is a hard
FAILURE.
MEASURED on the lab (Firebird 5.0.4) 2026-08-12, because the drivers diverge
and none of this may be assumed:
* Python firebird-driver: cursor.rowcount is the REAL affected count for
UPDATE/DELETE (3/0), -1 for INSERT; blobs arrive as memoryview -> bytes.
* Ruby fb gem: Fb::Connection#execute RETURNS the affected row count as an
Integer (1/2/0); blobs SUB_TYPE 0 arrive as a raw String.
* Node node-firebird: query()/execute() give NO affected count for DML
(callback result is undefined), BUT Firebird 5 multi-row RETURNING does
surface every affected row, so `... RETURNING *` + rows.length IS the real
count; a blob arrives as a STREAMING FUNCTION, never a Buffer, so it must
be read out; SRP login over WireCrypt is intermittently flaky (~12%
historically), so connect() carries a bounded retry.
* PHP: on PHP 8 ext-interbase's native path is present but the shipped
libfbclient cannot always negotiate SRP/WireCrypt; Database::create picks
the native FirebirdAdapter, which reads ibase_affected_rows() and a
RETURNING row for the last-id. pdo_firebird is the documented fallback.
FB-DEC-02 (generator last-id + real affected count). The audit framed the
write-contract gap as Ruby/Node-only, but MEASURING db.insert()/update()/
delete() through the public facade on real Firebird showed it broken in ALL
FOUR (drift reported): db.insert().last_id was None/0/nil/null everywhere, and
the affected count was fabricated (Node hardcoded 1) or wrong (PHP native read
ibase_affected_rows() from the LINK's implicit transaction instead of the
long-lived READ COMMITTED transaction the statement actually ran on -> 0). The
uniform contract, pinned four-way: db.insert(table, data) returns a
DatabaseResult whose last_id is the GENERATOR-assigned primary key (each
adapter reads GEN_ID(GEN_<TABLE>_ID, 0) after the INSERT, or -- Python -- via
the INSERT ... RETURNING * emulation) and whose affected_rows is 1; a second
insert returns the NEXT id; update/delete report the EXACT rows changed (a
multi-row change reports N, a no-match reports 0). Firebird-adapter-local in
every language; ZERO new runtime deps. Mutation-proved: fabricate the count /
drop the generator read -> the matching case goes RED.
FB-DEC-02 (non-`id` PK). Only Python EMULATES RETURNING (it strips the clause
and re-selects the inserted row); it re-selected by a HARDCODED `id` column
(`... WHERE id = ?`), so a table whose PK is NOT named `id` raised a Firebird
'Dynamic SQL Error' -- MEASURED. Python now re-selects by the table's REAL
primary key (introspected + cached + quoted), the same defect+fix features 10
and 11 applied to mysql.py and mssql.py. The generator last-id itself is
COLUMN-NAME-INDEPENDENT (GEN_ID reads the sequence, not a column), so a
non-`id`-PK insert already returns the right last-id in all four -- pinned
four-way as `firebird-nonid-pk-generated-id`. The Python-only re-select fix is
additionally witnessed by the Python suite's returning_* test (revert -> the
'WHERE id' Dynamic SQL Error RED).
FB-DEC-03 (blob + SRP). A binary blob carrying a NUL byte and high bytes
round-trips byte-for-byte through db.insert + a read back on a SECOND fresh
connection -- exactly what a naive text decode or an unread blob handle
corrupts. This is where Node's decodeBlobs no-op (it returned the driver's
streaming blob FUNCTION unchanged, asserting-not-verifying a Buffer) is fixed:
the adapter now reads the blob stream into a Buffer. node-firebird's flaky SRP
handshake is handled by a BOUNDED retry inside connect() (a transient
handshake failure recovers; a genuine bad credential still fails after the
bound -- never skipped, never papered over).
FB-DEC-01 (real reconnect, the no-mock rule -- non-negotiable). The Ruby
reconnect spec used RSpec doubles (`allow(driver).to receive(:open_connection)`)
to fake a Firebird server, so the reconnect path was proven only against a
mock -- a direct violation of the project's absolute no-mock rule, and in fact
NONE of the four frameworks had a real end-to-end reconnect test (Python
monkeypatched, PHP was matcher-only + a manual-QA note, Node had no reconnect
at all). This invariant is that test, REAL in every language: open a real
connection, force a server-side disconnect (DELETE FROM MON$ATTACHMENTS on the
adapter's own attachment id, from a second connection -> Firebird raises
'Connection shutdown' -- MEASURED), and prove the adapter transparently
reconnects so the NEXT query succeeds. A logical SQL error (a syntax error) is
the negative control: it must NOT trigger a reconnect (retrying would mask the
bug). Node gains a reconnect path (dead-connection markers + one-shot
re-attach + retry, skipped inside an explicit transaction) to match
Python/PHP/Ruby -- the parity gap the feature doc named is closed.
FB-COLUMN-CASE-TRAP (documented, inherent -- no code fix). Firebird folds an
UNQUOTED identifier to UPPERCASE (`CREATE TABLE foo` stores FOO; `SELECT 1 AS
x` returns column X), while a QUOTED identifier keeps its case (`AS "MyCol"`
stays MyCol). Every adapter folds an ALL-CAPS column name back to lowercase
for portability so row["x"] works across engines, and preserves a quoted
mixed-case name -- but a genuinely-quoted ALL-CAPS name (`AS "MYCOL"`) is
INDISTINGUISHABLE from a folded one and is lowercased too. That single spelling
cannot round-trip; it is inherent to Firebird's asymmetric folding, not a Tina4
bug, and is documented rather than 'fixed' (a fix would need to track quoting
through the whole query). Unquoted-folds-to-UPPERCASE is the rule to remember.
Env contract (canonical TINA4_TEST_FIREBIRD_* convention, identical to the
other live Firebird tests): TINA4_TEST_FIREBIRD_URL (an embedded-credential
URL, e.g. firebird://SYSDBA:masterkey@127.0.0.1:3050//var/lib/firebird/data/
tina4_<fw>.fdb). Unset -> the suite SKIPS cleanly (green) -- a machine with no
Firebird is the skip case, not the design. Firebird is EXCLUDED from the
require-services CI gate (GitHub CI provisions no Firebird); coverage is
LAB-ONLY and enforced there, which is what the CLAUDE.md claims now say
accurately (FB-GATE-EXCLUDED). Node's node-firebird driver is declared an
optionalDependency of @tina4/orm, not a devDependency.
feature: 12 - Firebird provider (FB-DEC-01 real reconnect replacing the Ruby no-mock violation; FB-DEC-02 generator-derived last-id + real affected-count through db.insert/update/delete four-way, and Python's real-PK RETURNING re-select for a non-`id` PK; FB-DEC-03 byte-for-byte blob round-trip, bounded SRP-login retry, and the case-fold trap documented), against a real Firebird 5

invariants.rule: On a real Firebird, db.insert(table, data) into a table whose id is assigned by a BEFORE INSERT trigger from a GEN_<TABLE>_ID generator returns a DatabaseResult whose last_id is the generator-assigned key (each adapter derives it -- Python via the INSERT ... RETURNING * emulation, PHP via native RETURNING *, Ruby/Node via a GEN_ID(GEN_<TABLE>_ID, 0) read after the INSERT) and whose affected_rows is 1; a SECOND insert returns the NEXT generated id, never a stale earlier one; the row is durably keyed and read back on a SECOND fresh connection. Identical in all four (Python Database.insert -> FirebirdAdapter; PHP Database::insert -> FirebirdAdapter; Ruby Database#insert -> FirebirdDriver; Node Database.insert -> FirebirdAdapter).
invariants.why: FB-LASTID-GAP: Firebird has no generic last_insert_id, so before this Ruby returned nil and Node returned null, while Python's db.insert() returned None (INSERT_RETURNING was empty so the generator emulation never fired) and PHP's native insert returned 0 (no RETURNING clause on the native path) -- MEASURED, so the gap was four-way, not the Ruby/Node the audit named. Each adapter now derives the generator key so db.insert().last_id is the real new id in all four. Mutation-proved: drop the generator read (Ruby/Node) / the RETURNING clause (Python/PHP) -> the last-id cases go RED. No mocks.
cases: an insert returns the generator last id
a second insert returns the next generated id
an insert reports affected rows of one

invariants.rule: On a real Firebird, db.update(...) and db.delete(...) return a DatabaseResult whose affected_rows is the EXACT number of rows changed: a multi-row update over a matching predicate reports N, an update whose predicate matches nothing reports 0, and a multi-row delete reports the number removed. Read the real count from the driver (Python cursor.rowcount, Ruby the Fb::Connection#execute return, PHP ibase_affected_rows() on the transaction that ran the statement, Node the row count of a `... RETURNING *`). Identical observable in all four.
invariants.why: FB-AFFECTED-FAB: Node FABRICATED affectedRows:1 on every insert/update/delete regardless of rows touched, Ruby had no affected_rows so the facade defaulted it, and PHP's native adapter read ibase_affected_rows() off the LINK's implicit transaction rather than the long-lived READ COMMITTED transaction the write actually ran on -> 0 (MEASURED; the 'best-effort, not verified against live Firebird' comment was the tell). All four now report the driver's real count. Proven with a multi-row change and a zero-match negative. Mutation-proved: restore the hardcoded 1 (Node) / read the wrong tx handle (PHP) -> the count and zero-match cases go RED. No mocks.
cases: a multi row update reports the real affected count
an update matching no rows reports zero affected
a delete reports the real affected count

invariants.rule: On a real Firebird, a binary blob (bytes carrying a NUL byte and high bytes 0xFD..0xFF) written into a BLOB SUB_TYPE 0 column via db.insert round-trips BYTE-FOR-BYTE when read back on a SECOND fresh connection. The adapter reads the blob out to the language's raw-bytes type (Python bytes, PHP string, Ruby String, Node Buffer). Identical observable in all four.
invariants.why: FB-BLOB-SRP-UNVERIFIED: Node's decodeBlobs was a no-op that ASSERTED node-firebird returns Buffers; MEASURED, a BLOB column arrives as a STREAMING FUNCTION, so the raw function leaked to the caller and no bytes round-tripped -- it now reads the stream into a Buffer. Python/PHP/Ruby already materialise the blob (memoryview->bytes / resource->string / String), pinned here so it can never regress. A NUL + high-byte payload is exactly what a text decode corrupts. Mutation-proved: revert Node's decode -> the blob case goes RED (the payload is a function, not bytes). No mocks.
cases: a binary blob round trips byte for byte

invariants.rule: On a real Firebird, after the adapter's own attachment is force-disconnected server-side (DELETE FROM MON$ATTACHMENTS on its MON$ATTACHMENT_ID, issued from a SECOND connection -> Firebird's next statement on the dead attachment raises 'Connection shutdown'), the adapter transparently reconnects on the next query and that query SUCCEEDS -- outside an explicit transaction. A logical SQL error (a syntax error) is the negative control: it is NOT a dead-connection marker, so it must surface to the caller WITHOUT a reconnect. Real Firebird, no test double.
invariants.why: FB-RUBY-MOCK (the no-mock violation, non-negotiable): Ruby's firebird_reconnect_spec faked the server with RSpec doubles, so the reconnect/retry path was proven only against a mock; and in fact no framework had a real end-to-end reconnect test. This is that test, real in every language against a genuinely killed connection. Node gains the reconnect path itself (dead-connection markers + one-shot re-attach + retry, skipped inside a transaction) so the invariant is four-way. Mutation-proved: neutralise the reconnect (return the dead handle) -> the reconnect case goes RED; make the matcher treat a syntax error as dead -> the negative case goes RED. No mocks.
cases: a forced disconnect reconnects and the next query succeeds
a logical sql error does not trigger a reconnect

invariants.rule: On a real Firebird, db.insert() into a table whose PRIMARY KEY is NOT named `id` (its key assigned by a GEN_<TABLE>_ID generator via a BEFORE INSERT trigger) returns a DatabaseResult whose last_id is the generator-assigned key -- the generator read is COLUMN-NAME-INDEPENDENT, so this is green four-way. Identical in all four.
invariants.why: FB-RETURNING-ID: the user-observable symptom of Python's hardcoded-`id` RETURNING emulation was 'an insert into a table whose PK is not id returns a wrong/no last-id'. Only Python emulates RETURNING (re-selecting the inserted row), and it fetched `... WHERE id = ?`, raising a Firebird 'Dynamic SQL Error' on a non-`id` PK (MEASURED). Python now re-selects by the table's REAL introspected+quoted primary key (the feature-10/11 fix shared with mysql.py/mssql.py). This case pins the correct observable four-way; the Python-only re-select fix is additionally witnessed by the Python suite's returning_* test (revert -> the 'WHERE id' Dynamic SQL Error RED). No mocks.
cases: a non id primary key insert returns the generated last id
